title: How the Papacy Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain the papacy: what the pope does, Pope Benedict XVI's (transcript says Benedict the Second, Joseph Ratzinger) retirement announced February 11, 2013, the precedent of Gregory XII retiring to end the Great Schism, the claim of Peter as first pope via Matthew 16:18, papal infallibility from the First Vatican Council (1870), the death and funeral process (Camerlengo, hammer tap, Ring of the Fisherman destroyed, triple coffin burial), the conclave of cardinal electors (age limit 80, two-thirds vote, ballots burned with chemical for black or white smoke), the acceptance ceremony and "Habemus Papam," and the origin of papal name changes with John II. The episode closes with a listener mail from Anne Marie, a veterinarian from Newfoundland, Canada, who listened during maternity leave.

segments.title: Opening banter and Benedict's retirement announcement
segments.summary: The hosts joke about the studio, then introduce the topic. They discuss Pope Benedict's February 11 announcement that he would retire, his background, and comparisons to John Paul II.

segments.title: Papacy defined and precedent for retirement
segments.summary: The hosts define the papacy and the pope's titles. They note Gregory XII was the last pope to retire, around 600 years earlier, ending the Great Schism, during which popes sat in Rome and Avignon.

segments.title: Papal succession from St. Peter
segments.summary: The hosts describe Peter as the first pope in church teaching, citing Matthew 16:18 and Jesus's instruction to feed his sheep. Peter was martyred in Rome under Nero and buried on Vatican Hill. Later popes are considered his successors.

segments.title: Papal infallibility and the pope's power
segments.summary: The First Vatican Council in 1870 declared the pope infallible in matters of faith and doctrine. The hosts compare the pope's role as leader of about 1.2 billion Catholics with Islam's lack of a single figurehead.

segments.title: Death of the pope and the camerlengo
segments.summary: When a pope dies, the Camerlengo, the Vatican's secretary of state, takes over non-theological duties. The death is confirmed by calling the pope's name, and the Ring of the Fisherman is destroyed with a silver hammer. The body lies in repose for nine days, and the pope is buried in three nested coffins.

segments.title: Conclave and papal balloting
segments.summary: Cardinal electors (under 80, up to 120) are sequestered in conclave until a two-thirds vote is reached. Ballots are written, read by scrutineers, strung on thread, and burned. Black smoke signals no decision and white smoke signals a new pope.

segments.title: Acceptance, Habemus Papam, and papal names
segments.summary: The elected pope accepts and chooses a name. Cardinals pay homage, and the senior cardinal announces Habemus Papam from the balcony. The hosts explain that the tradition of changing names began with John II, and that popes often choose a predecessor or favorite saint.

segments.title: Papal duties and Popemobile
segments.summary: The hosts list papal duties such as appointing bishops and cardinals and writing official documents. They note past papal influence over emperors, including Charlemagne's coronation, and mention the Popemobile.

segments.title: Listener mail from Anne Marie
segments.summary: A listener from Newfoundland, Canada, a veterinarian, says she discovered the show during maternity leave and listens while doing work. The hosts sign off with requests for feedback and website details.
